value.claim: Migration 0052 adds a nullable `role_type` to `community_assignments`. Assign stamps it from the role document the assign already reads.

The stamp is a cache of the role document's `meta.type`, refreshed at every point pij changes a type: `edit --type` restamps the role's open holdings in the same call; `retype --apply` (plan 238) does the same; the governance rebuild recomputes every row. A hand edit of the governance branch is the only way it can go stale, and the next rebuild refreshes it; `pij directory` reads the documents themselves, so the view is never stale.

Each seat in `pij list --json` gains `type` (the one type of its open holdings; with none, `prime` for the designated prime, `project-manager` for a `pm` seat, `pa` for a `pa` seat, else null; with two different types, null) and `types` (every distinct type it holds, sorted). Each holder row and role row in `pij directory --json` gains `type`. No existing field is removed or renamed, and the human list shows the type.
A seat whose open holdings carry two different types is a `pij directory` action naming both roles and the release line that splits them.
Every existing permission test passes unchanged: a knowledge-role seat and a coder-role seat show different types and the same worker authority.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: Seats are listed by GET /v1/seats (crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs) and joined to their seat role by `join_roles` (http/role.rs); community holdings are `community_assignments` (crates/store/src/community.rs). The view is built in community/directory.rs and its actions in community/picture.rs. The OMP and Copilot extensions read `pij list` JSON; new fields are additive.

value.risk: A stale stamp after a hand edit.
value.mitigation: Stated refresh point: the rebuild. The view reads documents directly.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Cost: migration 0052: one ALTER at boot. One extra column written per assign and per restamp (edit --type, retype --apply, rebuild). `pij list` reads the column from the holding rows it already joins: 0 launches, no file read. No loop, poll or timer.
No permission rule changes (PRD 003); no daemon enforcement of a type's rules; no existing JSON field removed or renamed.
Builds nice-19 through `just shared-build`, one at a time.
